SEO Content Writing

How to Write Blog Posts That Rank and Get Read

Ranking content starts with understanding what the searcher needs, then answering it more clearly and completely than anyone else. Here’s the process.

VXVintorex Digital team3 min read · Evergreen guide

Key takeaways

  • Choose topics your customers actually search for and that relate to what you sell.
  • Study the current top results to understand the intent and the expected depth.
  • Structure for skimming: clear headings, short paragraphs, lists and examples.
  • Add original experience and insight. It is what makes content worth ranking.

1. Pick the right topic

Good topics sit at the overlap of three things: questions your customers ask, phrases people search for, and subjects connected to your services. Sources of ideas include sales and support questions, reviews, keyword research tools, and the “people also ask” style questions in search results.

2. Understand search intent

Search your target phrase and study the top results. Are they guides, lists, product pages or comparisons? How deep do they go? Which questions do they all answer, and which do they miss? Your article should match the expected format and then do better on clarity, completeness or originality.

3. Outline before writing

  • A title that includes the main topic and promises a clear benefit.
  • An introduction that confirms the reader is in the right place and says what they will learn.
  • Headings that cover the questions a reader will have, in a logical order.
  • A conclusion with a clear next step.

4. Write for skimmers and readers

Most people scan first. Clear structure decides whether they stay to read.
  • Use short paragraphs and plain language.
  • Use descriptive subheadings that make sense on their own.
  • Use bullet lists for steps, features and checklists.
  • Use examples, numbers you can verify, and visuals where they help.
  • Define jargon the first time you use it.

5. Add what only you can add

Generic content is everywhere. Your advantage is experience: real examples from your work, mistakes you see customers make, photos of your process, opinions backed by practice. This is what makes content credible to readers and valuable to search engines.

6. On-page optimisation

  • Use the main topic in the title, the main heading, the opening paragraph and at least one subheading, naturally.
  • Write a compelling meta description that summarises the benefit.
  • Use a short, readable URL.
  • Link to related articles and relevant service pages on your site.
  • Add descriptive image alt text.
  • Add FAQ or how-to structured data where appropriate.

7. Edit ruthlessly

Read it aloud. Cut repetition, filler and vague claims. Check facts and links. Make sure every section earns its place.

8. Publish, promote and refresh

Share new posts on social media and in your newsletter, and link to them from related pages. Review older posts periodically. Update outdated sections, improve weak ones and merge overlapping articles. Refreshing good content is often more effective than publishing more.

Frequently asked questions

How long should a blog post be?

As long as it takes to answer the question well. Match the depth that searchers and the current top results suggest. Padding for length makes content worse.

How often should I publish?

Consistency matters more than volume. A regular rhythm of genuinely useful posts, such as weekly or fortnightly, beats bursts of rushed content.
